You drop the bishop back to a safe and strong square. Exactly right — 0 loss.
Black takes the pawn, opening that fatal diagonal. You must recapture, but the rook in the corner is now in danger.
Black defends his back rows with the rook. A bit passive for him; keep pressing.

Black offers a queen trade. Since you are fighting to simplify, this is interesting for you.

White develops the other knight to c3. Nothing scary — keep getting your pieces out.
White pushes e5 to kick your knight. Don't panic; jump the knight forward to a strong square.

White checks with Ng5+, but it's just a bluff with no follow-up. Simply step the king back.
Kg8 returns your king to safety. Well played.

They bring the knight out. Now is the perfect time for the d5 break.
They trade pawns in the middle. Just take back and keep your nice center.
Big blunder! They give up the bishop for nothing real. Just take it: Kxh7 wins a whole piece for free.
Their rook steps next to your bishop. You can simply trade it off.
Re8 is fine but not best. Nxc1 wins the bishop in the corner for free. Lesson: always scan for an enemy piece you can just take.
Their knight jumps to b5 eyeing your pawns. Defend calmly and keep your rooks active.

White trades knights. After you recapture, your bishop will be active. No problem for you.
Good — the queen retreats safely to d8. You lose a little time but stay solid.
White puts the rook on e1, eyeing your pawn on e5. Defend calmly and finish getting your king safe.
Good — the king moves to c7, the right square. Keep finding safe king moves.
Good — king to b8, staying safe. White cannot make real progress if you keep finding the right squares.

Good — king to b8 again, holding firm. You are defending the checks well.
Black takes your pawn, which is expected. Take it back with your knight next.
Your queen move drifts a bit; Qd4 was better, sitting strong in the center. Lesson: put your queen where it controls the most squares.

Black shuffles his queen back. You can jump your knight to a4 to poke at him.

Nd2 reroutes your knight to a better post. A calm, useful move.

Black blocks with Kf7. Now collect the bishop you can take.

Great — your queen steps back safely and now aims at White's weak d3 pawn.

White's rook attacks your bishop on d3. Keep your bishop and knight safe.
Clever — your knight forks White's rook in the corner. This is the best move.

Good — your rook guards your second rank. This is basically the best move.

White plays a quiet pawn to d3. This is passive. You should strike in the center now while you can.
White trades pawns with exd5. Just take back so your center stays solid.

White develops the knight to f3. Normal. Just keep getting your pieces out and think about castling.

Bb5+ gives a check but it is a weak move. The bishop will just get chased away soon. Block it with c6 like the engine wants.
Nf3 develops his knight. Normal move, nothing scary.
Be7 develops the bishop and gets you ready to castle. Fine and safe.
Nf3 brings his knight back. No threat to you. Keep developing.
Bf5 develops the bishop with tempo. Castling first was a touch better, but this is fine.
Na3 develops his other knight to the side. No real threat. Carry on.
Ke1 just steps the king over. Your knight is still busy in his camp.
Kf1 walks toward your knight in the corner. Careful — that knight on h1 can get trapped later.
Qf4 eyes your kingside. Stay calm and get your king out.

Kg1 steps back. No danger.

Kb5 dodges. Stay with the checks.

Qe8+ checks your king. Block it.

Kb7 steps over. Keep going.
Kc7 steps aside. Keep checking.

Their bishop retreats to b3. Keep rolling your pawns — c5 next is strong.

You retreat the rook to d8. Safe and sound.
They double rooks on c1. Stay active — keep your rooks on good files.
Your rook comes to e8. A fine, calm move keeping pressure.

Your bishop returns to a6. Good — it watches the queening square.

Your king goes to h7. Safe, the knight check leads nowhere.
You recapture on c2. Good, your rook is still deep in their camp.
Their king steps to f1. Keep probing — Rh2 keeps the rook active.
Your rook swings to h2, grabbing the h-pawn next. Best, keeps the pressure.
You push a5, starting your passed pawn's run. Right plan to finish the game.
You push a4, closer to making a queen. Keep it rolling.

White brings a rook over. Stay calm and keep your pieces safe — your queen should head back home soon.

You move your king to d8, the best square. Your king is a bit exposed but holding.

Their rook drops back to keep checking distance. Keep pushing your kingside pawns.
Good, you push g5 to drive your passed pawns forward — that is your winning plan.

Good, you push g6 to keep the passed pawns running at their king.

Black's bishop steps to d4. You can simply swap it off.
Knight to e4 — well done. It eyes great central squares.

Knight back to e4. Small step; Nb3 was a touch better. Still fine.

Black's queen swings to f5, eyeing your king. Get pieces back to defend and stay calm.

They pin your knight with Bb5. Stay calm — centralize your queen to d5 and you are fine.

You push h4. Doubling rooks on the e-file was more useful, but no harm done.

They block with Kf1. You are still clearly winning — bring the queen to f3 and keep pressing for the finish.

Your rook lines up on the e-file for a future push. Fine; a6 (stopping White's knight jump) was also nice.
White trades pawns in the middle. Just take back.
White trades the pawns. Take back with the c-pawn.
White's knight leaps to a central square and offers a trade.
King to h8 keeps you safe and your bishop still hunts the queen. Cool head, well done.
